documentation.description:
Options:
  --format FORMAT      Select one format: RGB565, RGB888, RGB8888.
                       The default is RGB565.
  --background R,G,B   Set the background for transparent pixels.
                       Use 0-255 per channel. The default is 0,0,0.
  --type-package PACKAGE
                       Use the types from this package. Also set
                       --pixel-type and --array-type.
  --pixel-type TYPE    Set the pixel type in --type-package.
  --array-type TYPE    Set the array type in --type-package.
  <input.png>          Give the required PNG file.
  [output-name]        Set the Ada package name. By default, png_embed
                       uses the input file name without its extension.
  --help, -h           Show this help.
Options.Parse and Put_Pixel support all three formats.

record_types.name: RGB_Color

documentation.description:
The pixel-array type's name, declared in Type_Package_Name.
Empty unless Uses_External_Type. Parse exits with an error if
this is not a legal Ada identifier.
The input PNG file's path, as given on the command line.

The .ads file name GNAT expects for Output_Pkg_Name: the name
in lower case, with ".ads" appended.

The Ada package name for the generated file: the name given on
the command line, if any, otherwise Input_File_Name's base name
(extension stripped). Parse exits with an error instead if that
name, given or derived, is not already a legal Ada
identifier. Does not check for reserved words.

Parses Ada.Command_Line and sets the options.

Returns normally only when parsing succeeded
On --help/-h, or on a bad argument, Parse prints a
help message and exits.

The one-pixel type's name, declared in Type_Package_Name. Empty
unless Uses_External_Type. Parse exits with an error if this is
not a legal Ada identifier.

The package to `with` in the generated file. Empty unless
Uses_External_Type. Parse exits with an error if this is not a
legal Ada name (a dotted child-unit name is accepted).

True when the user gave --type-package, --pixel-type, and
--array-type together. Then the generated file `with`s
Type_Package_Name and uses its Pixel_Type_Name/Array_Type_Name
for one pixel and for the whole array. False (the default)
means png_embed declares its own RGB565/RGB565_Array types in
the generated file.
